title: Ballet
author: Daniel Kimber
body: Deterministic AI workflow automation for Ops teams

draft.why: B2B SaaS launching on PH targeting Ops teams; founders who launch here often need landing page and onboarding design help soon after.
options: Congrats on the launch. Curious who the ideal first user is: the Ops lead building the workflows, or the engineers who currently get pulled in to maintain them? That answer changes a lot about how you should onboard people.

Congrats on shipping. My read is 'deterministic' is your sharpest differentiator against the agent-style automation tools, but are you finding Ops buyers actually know that word, or do you translate it into a reliability promise on the landing page?

draft.why: Recall.ai is a funded B2B dev-tool company with a real launch audience, and launch threads attract founders who hire design help.
options: Congrats on the launch. Curious who you expect to build on this first: teams adding meeting features to existing products, or folks building standalone meeting agents from scratch?

Congrats on shipping. My read is the hardest sell isn't the API itself but trust on the other side of the call, since the bot shows up as a participant. Is the positioning aimed at use cases where attendees already expect a notetaker, or are you betting people get comfortable with agents joining cold?

title: polyroom
author: Rodrigo Lemela Duarte
body: Where AI agents work together and your team decides

draft.why: AI collaboration tool launch with an unclear audience, so a sharp positioning question could surface a founder conversation
options: Congrats on launching! Quick question on the first-run experience: when someone signs up, do they start by setting up the agents themselves or by inviting their team first? That choice says a lot about who the product is really for.

The tagline splits the focus between agents and the team, which makes me wonder about positioning. Is the buyer an engineering lead managing AI workflows, or a non-technical team trying to delegate tasks to agents? Curious because the messaging probably needs to pick one first.

title: infaiw
author: Dipankar Das
body: Delegate work to sidecar agents that pass an approval script

draft.why: PH launch for an AI agent tool; founder is likely technical and reachable, and approval-flow UX is a real design surface.
options: Congrats on the launch. Who's the first user you built this for: dev teams automating internal ops, or non-technical folks delegating tasks? The approval script idea sounds powerful but I'm curious how you make it feel safe on a first run.

Quick question on positioning: are you pitching this as 'agents you can trust' or 'agents you can audit'? The approval script angle suggests the second, which feels like a sharper wedge against the flood of autonomous agent tools. Curious which one resonates in your early conversations.

title: Pinecall
author: Bernardo Castro
body: The open-source platform for voice AI agents

draft.why: PH launch for an open-source voice AI platform, likely dev-facing, so low direct fit for Ryan's B2B SaaS design work, but founders in comments may be relevant.
options: Congrats on the launch! Curious who you're picturing as the first user here: is it developers prototyping voice agents for fun, or teams shipping production phone agents at companies? The answer probably changes what the first-run experience should look like.

Happy launch day! Honest question on positioning: with the space this crowded, is open source the main hook, or is there a specific use case (like support calls or outbound) where you think Pinecall beats the closed platforms? That answer probably deserves to be front and center in the tagline.
